content.title: Special Event Permit for Olde Town Arvada
content.summary: To host a special event in Olde Town Arvada, applicants must adhere to specific guidelines, including no vehicle parking on Town Square and restrictions on sidewalk chalk and generator placement. Required documentation includes a general liability insurance certificate, a detailed site plan, a parking plan, and a waste clean-up plan, with an emphasis on using recyclable or compostable materials for food and beverage service. Additional requirements may apply if alcohol is served, and applicants are encouraged to contact Risk Management for further clarification.
content.body:
Planning an event outside of Olde Town? If you have not already read the guidelines for applying for [Special Event Permits](/663/Special-Event-Permits), please be sure to do so. You'll find information on races, park events, and more.

## Before You Begin

The following rules apply to all special events held in Olde Town

- Olde Town Square: There is no vehicle parking allowed on Town Square
- Olde Town Fountain: Fountain remains open to the public. Exceptions may apply.
- Sidewalk Chalk: Sidewalk chalk is not allowed to be used on surfaces in Olde Town.
- Electrical Outlets: Electricity is not available.
- Generator: Generators cannot be placed on turf.
- Petting Zoos: No petting zoo animals are allowed on turf.

## Checklist for Special Event Permits in Olde Town

### Items You Will Need

1. [Insurance Certificate](#tab2c6fb706-35bc-48a6-b2dd-e2d450372070_0)

Please request the following from your insurance agent or broker. They will issue the certificate:

- General Liability Certificate showing you (the Special Event applicant) as the Insured, in the minimum amount of $1,000,000 each occurrence
- The certificate holder box and additional insured must read:  
  The City of Arvada  
  Risk Management  
  8101 Ralston Road  
  Arvada, CO 80002
- Policy coverage must include the date(s) of the event(s)

If alcoholic beverages are served, additional requirements apply. Note that these are the minimum requirements. Additional insurance may be required as determined solely by Risk Management for the City of Arvada. If you have questions, please contact Risk Management, 720-898-7590

1. [Site Plan](#tab2c6fb706-35bc-48a6-b2dd-e2d450372070_1)

## Site Plan Instructions

A detailed sitemap of your event should show the following, if applicable:

- Event route Start/Finish points
- Event registration points
- Stage and sound equipment placement
- Food and/or beverage tent (size and location)
- Merchandise tents (size and location)
- Banner and/or signage size and placement
- First aid/medical sites
- Parking locations
- Generator particulars and locations. Not to be placed on turf.
- Street closure points
- Location of any special attractions
- Electricity requirements

![Event Site Plan Example](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=939)Example:

1. [Parking Plan](#tab2c6fb706-35bc-48a6-b2dd-e2d450372070_2)

Event coordinator will need to supply the following information:

- Public parking spaces that will be closed or significantly impacted
- Location of vendor parking
- Location of patron parking
- Plans for shuttling patrons or vendors from outlying parking areas
- Letter or signature from any private property owner who is allowing for event parking
- Promotional strategies for notifying participants of the parking plan (promotional materials should encourage participants to get to the event using an alternate travel mode ex. train, bike, walk, bus)

1. [Waste Clean-Up Plan](#tab2c6fb706-35bc-48a6-b2dd-e2d450372070_3)

A waste plan should be included with your application outlining the type of waste that will be generated, steps that will be taken to reduce the amount of waste from the event, i.e. recycling containers and how the waste will be disposed of which may mean the need for temporary dumpsters.

Sustain Arvada is committed to making sure that environmentally friendly events are hosted within the City of Arvada. With that, the City requires all food vendors to serve food and drinks in recyclable or compostable containers. Examples of compliant products include:

- Compostable food containers
- Plates, cold and hot cups, straws, food containers, cutlery, napkins, boxes and bags (made from paper, natural fiber or bio plastic). If using bio-plastic it must be labeled as compostable and be approved for composting.
- Recyclable food containers
- Clean paper
- Aluminum/steel cans
- Aluminum foil
- Cardboard
- Glass bottles
- Plastic bottles

### Items You Will Need If

1. [Tax Exempt Number (You Are a Non-Profit)](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_0)

If your organization is a non-profit (501(c)(3)), you will need to provide your Tax Exempt Number. Your TIN is **not** your EIN. For more information, please visit the [Colorado Department of Revenue](https://www.colorado.gov/revenue).

1. [Residential Street Closure Permit (You Are Closing a Residential Street)](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_1)

If you are holding an event that will require the closure of a residential street, you will be required to submit a Residential Street Closure Permit. The permit requires you provide approval signatures of 80% of the residents who will be affected by the closure.

In order to apply for a Residential Street Closure, you will need to complete a [Request for Revocable Temporary Street Closure Packet (PDF)](/DocumentCenter/View/938).

1. [Commercial Street Closure Permit (You Are Closing a Commercial Street)](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_2)

If you are holding an event which will require the closure of any street in a commercial area, you will need to apply for a Commercial Street Closure Permit. You will need to provide a list of business affected by the closure along with approval signatures from 80% of affected business owners.

In order to apply for a Commercial Street Closure, you will need to complete a [Request for Revocable Temporary Street Closure for Commercial Neighborhoods packet (PDF)](/DocumentCenter/View/938).

1. [Vendor List](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_3)

Vendors selling merchandise are required to collect and remit sales tax to the City of Arvada. Special Event Coordinators are responsible for providing Revenue with a finalized vendor list before the start of the event. The vendor list should include all of the following information:

- Business Name
- Business Address
- Contact Name
- Contact Phone
- Contact Email

Revenue staff will provide the special event coordinator with a partially personalized tax form. The coordinator distributes the form to all vendors. Vendors participating in a special event **are not required** to have a business license, as they are covered under the special event.

1. [Vendor Certificate of Liability Coverage (Event Includes Bounce Houses)](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_4)

In addition to the insurance certificate required by all special event applicants, applicants whose event includes outside vendors are also required to provide evidence of the vendor's liability coverage. Examples are:

- Food trucks or tent vendors
  - General Liability in the minimum amount of $1,000,000
  - Products and Completed Operations of $1,000,000
- Beer or Alcohol vendors
  - General Liability in the minimum amount of $1,000,000
  - Products and Completed Operations of $1,000,000
  - Liquor Liability of $1,000,000
- Inflatables or mechanicals such as bounce houses, amusement rides)
  - General Liability in the minimum amount of $1,000,000
  - Products and Completed Operations of $1,000,000
- Entertainment and staging (if separate from the Special Event applicant)
  - General Liability in the minimum amount of $1,000,000
  - Products and Completed Operations of $1,000,000

Please obtain documentation of the vendor's liability coverage from the vendor.

- The certificate holder box and additional insured for all certificates must read:  
  The City of Arvada  
  Risk Management  
  8101 Ralston Road  
  Arvada, CO 80002
- Policy coverage must include the date(s) of the event(s)

**Note that these are the minimum requirements.** Additional insurance may be required as determined solely by Risk Management for the City of Arvada. If you have questions, please contact Risk Management, 720-898-7590.

1. [Alcohol Permit (Event Includes Alcohol)](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_5)

To ensure compliance with the City’s Designated Drinking Area (DDA) rules, all special event permit holders must implement the following measures:

## 1. Controlled Entry & Exit Points

- Permit holders must establish clearly defined and staffed entry and exit points for the event area.
- Staff or volunteers must actively monitor these access points.
- At all exits, patrons with alcohol must be instructed to “Drink It or Dump It” before leaving the designated area.
- Visible signage reinforcing this requirement must be posted at all exit points not already signed by the City.

## 2. Open Container Enforcement

- Patrons may not leave the Designated Drinking Area with open containers under any circumstances.
- If W. 57th Avenue remains open to vehicle traffic during the event, patrons:
  - May not cross the street with open containers
  - Must dispose of or finish beverages before crossing
- Staff or volunteers should help to enforce this rule.

## 3. Alcohol Source Restrictions

- Outside alcohol is strictly prohibited within the event and DDA boundaries. This includes alcohol purchased from a retail liquor store.
- Only alcohol purchased from Eligible Liquor Licensed Businesses (bars, restaurants, and tasting rooms with valid takeout permits) within the Entertainment District is permitted.
- Patrons must retain the official sticker with QR code on their beverage containers

## 4. Patron Education & Volunteer Support

- Permit holders must instruct volunteers or staff to:
  - Educate patrons about DDA rules and direct them to the QR code for further instructions
  - Direct patrons to signage and disposal locations
  - Encourage compliance in a friendly, proactive manner
- Volunteers should specifically remind patrons about:
  - “Drink It or Dump It” at exit points
  - No crossing streets with open containers
  - No outside alcohol

## 5. Signage Requirements

- Permit holders must ensure signage is posted at:
  - All entry points not already signed by the City (entering DDA rules apply)
  - All exit points not already signed by the City (“Drink It or Dump It”)
  - Key gathering areas and intersections not already signed by the City
- Signage should clearly state:
  - Open containers cannot leave the DDA
  - No outside alcohol allowed
  - Compliance is required by law

## 6. Compliance with Laws

- All event operations must comply with:
  - City of Arvada Municipal Code
  - State liquor laws
  - DDA administrative rules
- These requirements are in addition to any conditions in the Special Event Permit.

## 7. Enforcement & Consequences

- Failure to follow DDA rules may result in:
  - Open container violations issued to patrons
  - Enforcement action by police
  - Potential impacts to future event permitting
- Permit holders are expected to actively support compliance to minimize violations.

1. [Food Truck Guidelines (Event Includes Food Trucks)](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_6)

Each participating vendor will need to complete an application and supply the event coordinator with the appropriate documentation required (health certification). The event coordinator should consolidate the vendor applications and appropriate documentation and submit a complete set with their formal Special Event Permit application. Applicants will need to identify where each food truck will be set up within the event boundaries on the site plan/site map.

1. [Tent Permit](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_7)

The City of Arvada requires a tent permit if your event includes use of tents or temporary membrane structures that exceed 400 square-feet in area or any combination of smaller tents clustered together meeting the requirements above, will also need a permit: unless there is a 12 foot break between a cluster of smaller tents so that they do not exceed the 400 or 700 square foot requirement. Exception: Tents that are open on all sides do not require a permit unless they exceed 700 square-feet in area.

In order to apply for a Tent Permit, you will need to complete a Commercial Tenant Finish / Miscellaneous form.

The Arvada Fire Protection District (AFPD) will review the permit application for compliance with the City of Arvada adopted Fire Code. Please visit arvadafire.com to view the fire safety requirements. For more information call 303-424-3012.

1. [Course Route / Marshal Plan (Event Includes a Race)](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_8)

For foot races taking place in the public Right-of-Way, please submit a plan or drawing showing the race route and the locations of all course marshals and/or uniformed traffic control officers along the race route. Please specify if course marshals will be equipped with safety vests, **stop**paddles, flags, etc. Additional course marshals may be required as a condition of approval of the permit.

1. [Parade Route](#tab3cc5f6e4-f22c-437a-9ac4-28156e36db8d_9)

Include start and finish points and all streets to be traveled.

## Items You May Need After Review

1. [Emergency Medical Plan](#tab71880554-9354-416b-9342-50e8a66f0d80_0)

For information on what to provide in an Emergency Medical Plan, please [email Dave Mitchell](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#9ffbfee9fab1f2f6ebfcf7faf3f3dffeede9fefbfef9f6edfab1fcf0f2) Arvada Fire Protection District Emergency Medical Services Chief at 303-424-3012. Please see the contact options on [Arvada Fire Protection](http://arvadafire.com).

1. [Fire Safety Plan](#tab71880554-9354-416b-9342-50e8a66f0d80_1)

The event sponsor assumes overall responsibility for the setup and operation of the special event and ensures compliance with all fire and risk reduction guidelines and requirements. For information on what is required in a Fire Safety Plan, please visit the [Arvada Fire Protection District](http://arvadafire.com). For more information call 303-424-3012.

1. [Public Safety / Security (Off-Duty Police)](#tab71880554-9354-416b-9342-50e8a66f0d80_2)

If you want security at your event, or are required to have it after your application is reviewed, you have options.

## Hire Off-Duty Arvada Police Officers

Contact Arvada Police Department at 720-898-6663. There is a fee for this service.

## Hire Private Security

If you are hiring security, you may be asked to provide the security firm's name, contact details, and other information to the Arvada Police Department.

1. [Traffic Control Plan](#tab71880554-9354-416b-9342-50e8a66f0d80_3)

A Temporary Traffic Control Plan (TTCP) is required whenever any part of a special event will take place within any Arvada street. The TTCP shows how road users (including cars, trucks, buses, bikes, and pedestrians) will be informed about and guided through or around the special event zone. Usually this involves a combination of advance warning signs (Road Closed Ahead, Detour Ahead, etc), cones, barricades, flaggers, and detour signs. The TTCP is a computer generated plan that illustrates how and where all of those elements will be arranged. TTCPs are reviewed by Traffic Engineering staff and must meet specific guidelines for device type, size, and spacing. If your TTCP does not meet those requirements, your special event permit will not be granted. TTCPs require 2 to 3 business days for review, and hand-drawn plans are not accepted.

If a Traffic Control Plan is required for your event, contacting a traffic control company and requesting a TTCP is the often the best and easiest option. The City cannot recommend any specific company, but you can find many options on Google or in the Yellow Pages under "Traffic Control Company."

Example:![Traffic Control Plan Example](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=937)

## Applies to All Events

1. [Noise Ordinance Municipal Code Sec. 38-61](#tabf2fc6e86-c04f-4099-9687-44bfe3a00c7a_0)

Please review [Article II (Noise Control) on Municode](https://www.municode.com/library/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH38EN_ARTIINOCO).

## Online Application Process

- **Time:** Application must be submitted at least **60 days** prior to the event but not MORE than 12 months prior to the event.
- **Cost:**There is a **non-refundable $125** application fee (additional fees may apply).
- **Payment Types:** Online with Visa or Mastercard. Some fees may require payment by check.

The City of Arvada uses SMART License & Permits for the Special Event Permit application process.

- New to SMART License & Permits? View our [log in instructions and SMART License & Permits application guide](/665/Applying-for-a-Permit-with-SMART License & Permits).
- Returning User? [Login to the SMART License & Permits application]([NEW PORTAL URL]).

Utilize the [SMART License & Permits Application]([NEW PORTAL URL]).

## Contact

For information on the Special Event permitting process, please contact Community Development at 720-898-7435 or [email Planning Division](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#23534c47634251554247420d4c5144).
